procedures.title: PhD resource limits
procedures.summary: Records: submit_job and revise_job supply the actual proposed resource request at mutation. Positive approve_job reads the saved owner and request before its callback; dispatch_job reads them at mutation. Bounds are fixed rule constants.

reads.text: Submit/revise use actual proposed copied spec; positive approval/dispatch use saved owner/job spec. Bounds are static rule constants rather than saved quota configuration. Numeric Field emission accepts only exact Python int within signed int64.

steps.text: Rules: PhD requests must meet all limits: 1–8 CPU cores, 1–32 GB memory and 1–60 minutes runtime, inclusive. Missing or invalid numeric values and excess values prevent Allow rather than deriving QUOTA_EXCEEDED.

Positive approval accepts CPU or GPU within these limits. Submission and revision also need requested-node-type; dispatch needs physical-capacity. The broad numeric condition also supports Master effects, subject to Master limits.
Rejection is exempt. Direct approval mutation has no added resource check; the app's existing approval and candidate resource checks remain necessary and may additionally refuse.

procedures.title: Master resource limits

reads.text: Submit/revise select Master by actual caller and inspect proposed copied spec. Positive approval/dispatch select saved owner Master and saved job spec. Limits are static rule constants.

steps.text: Rules: Master requests require CPU and all limits: 1–4 CPU cores, 1–8 GB memory and 1–20 minutes runtime, inclusive. Positive approval uses this exact branch; rejection is exempt.

At submission, revision and dispatch, any cores >4, memory >8, runtime >20 or non-CPU type explicitly denies QUOTA_EXCEEDED, overriding broad numeric Allow. These denies select the caller for submission/revision and saved owner for dispatch.
The broad numeric check supplies lower bounds; missing or invalid numbers prevent Allow, not zero-fill. Ownership checks remain necessary. Direct approval mutation has no added resource bound.

procedures.title: PhD before an unaged Master
procedures.summary: Records: Before dispatch_job mutates, the gate reads target and contender state, approval evidence, resources, node type and waiting_dispatches. The counter starts at 0; only successful original dispatches increment other eligible same-type candidates.

reads.text: Priority deny requires broad Allow(target), a distinct queued competitor, and the approval joins/applied Professor witness in current-approval. Competitor uses same node type as target and must fit a free same-type node under physical-capacity, except rule64’s explicitly weaker branch. Its node witness can differ from target’s witness. Role-specific contender resource bounds are referenced per branch.

waiting_dispatches starts at 0 and submission_seq=len(jobs)+1. Only a successful original dispatch increments other currently eligible candidates of the selected node type; failed/blocked attempts or wall-clock time do not increment. Original candidates already apply saved quotas, approval policy digest and free-node checks.

steps.text: Rules: Given broad target Allow, a Master target with waiting_dispatches <3 is denied PRIORITY_CONFLICT if any distinct queued same-type PhD contender passes current-approval, PhD resource limits and physical-capacity. Its free-node witness may differ from the target's.

Missing contender or counter evidence prevents this Deny, not necessarily dispatch Allow. The threshold is fixed at 3 dispatch opportunities, not elapsed time or saved aging configuration; blocked attempts do not age jobs.

steps.text: Rules: Positive permission has no state restriction. A present state differing from all of QUEUED, RUNNING, COMPLETED and TERMINATED explicitly denies UNAVAILABLE. Missing state does not trigger this Deny and can reach an original state-access error.

QUEUED permits original termination without release. RUNNING permits a stop attempt subject to confirmation and nested release. COMPLETED or TERMINATED permits original ALREADY_TERMINAL no-op success, not an added refusal.

limitations: Static reconstruction of supplied installed enforcement only; no source policy, forward plan, actual trajectory or tests were supplied or executed. This does not establish intended-policy completeness or observed runtime success.

Composition is explicit Allow AND no matching Deny. Missing Allow is a refusal even without a named Deny. Local quota/state/priority denies can override positive branches. Adapter refusal projection masks private/unrecognized codes to UNAVAILABLE; read returns only status. Other refusal dictionaries include policy feedback. release_allocation/persistence/export raise ApplicationError; provider raises BackendError. Allowed original ok=False results remain delegated not-applied outcomes; original exceptions remain distinct from rule denials.

Installed binding has MECHANISMS=('capability','observations') and INVARIANTS=(). There is no added global FSM, lifecycle-state, task-hash, policy-digest, immutable-owner, allocation uniqueness or private-content invariant. The original offline audit runs after effects with intercepted=False; it is not added enforcement and cannot cancel an effect.

Framework integrity checks still enforce frozen call names/allowed supplied parameter keys/types, exact int64 numeric encodings, conflicting single-valued Field rejection, Event identity keys and append-only Event retention. These support business checks, not a separate workflow. Call contracts do not require absent declared keys; consuming rule joins do. All contract observedAt fields are None, so no observation TTL/freshness clock is installed.

Mutation gate state read/check/callback/SQLite commit is enclosed by original BEGIN IMMEDIATE. Interface snapshots are separate and not atomic with later callback reads. Layers have separate Policy instances for nesting. Framework successful bookkeeping may finish before outer SQLite commit; adapter approval/completion journal entries are appended only after original Store commit returns. An exception after a real effect can stop a policy session as execution_uncertain; framework failure is not general rollback of external effects.

Each gate rebuilds request-scoped snapshot fields plus the per-Store in-memory journal. Journal entries have no deliberate expiry but disappear with a fresh Store/Session. Invalid numeric Fields are omitted unless exact Python int within signed int64. Saved top-level/nested job spec conflicts can fail single-field validation; absent collections or malformed producers can raise rather than produce a business refusal. Snapshot is fingerprinted as complete by the adapter, not independently authenticated.

Trusted-process bypasses remain: unknown Trace.tool names return the original callback, generic unregistered Store._mutate is unwrapped, direct Store.view/read_job and fixture reads are not policy decorated, and SQL/state/wrapped-body/caller_context access is outside process isolation. Python can construct Tools/Trace actors; the host must protect identity binding. These bypasses affect the corresponding permission, ownership, quota, approval, completion and allocation checks.

No added free-text/private-context/influence guard exists. Bus.send wrapper observes original delivery and appends no content facts for authorization. Agent.decide wrapper sets _MODEL without a consuming content gate. Original audit may detect peer private strings after receipt/context exposure. Comments/prompts asserting isolation are not enforcement.

Credential scans cover only registered exact key strings at three named application boundaries. Framework telemetry may separately record arguments/results/state. visible_observation redacts configured keys only for the monitored model_output path, not all traces, payloads or files. Unknown credentials and all other sensitive content remain outside those rules.
